description: Deliver a persisted assistant message to the requester via the agent messaging bridge for the current session. Use this to send quick acknowledgements, status/progress updates, final answers, summaries of search results (with source attribution), completed work products, and error/clarification requests. This action is communication only: it does not execute tools, modify files, or create plan artifacts. The message is emitted as a channel_message event on the bound MCP bridge (Claude Code, Codex, or any other connected agent). Note: persisted conversation history includes a JSON metadata trailer appended by the platform (namespace/source/destination/posted_at/session_id/etc); do not include any metadata trailer or embedded JSON inside arguments.message. For multi-step goals, prefer create_extended_plan to produce the plan artifact that drives subsequent execution; status updates are fine, but they do not replace a plan artifact when one is needed.
embedding_description: Reply to the user with a final answer, status update, progress note, summary of search results with source attribution, or clarification question. Outbound prose message delivered to whichever MCP client started the current session (Claude Code, Codex). Terminal communication action. Persist the assistant turn and emit a channel_message event. No tool execution, no file changes, no plan artifacts.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Delivers a message to the connected agent through the agent_messaging bridge. post_message accepts {message, attachments?}.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: ValidationError: arguments do not conform to the schema. session_not_bound: no bridge session is bound to this session_id. APIError: the bridge rejected the enqueue (queue full, oversize message, or bridge closed).
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: Do not assume delivery succeeded when post_message fails. If session_not_bound, the originating MCP client has dropped its bridge — wait for it to reconnect or ask the operator to re-open the channel before continuing communication-dependent work. If APIError indicates the queue is full, retry later with a concise current-state update rather than flooding the channel. If the message is too large, send a shorter summary and defer details until a follow-up turn. ValidationError is a structural fault in the call site, not a transient condition — fix the arguments before retrying.
